use_case_summary: Main workload: clinical document retrieval for clinician-facing search UI (RAG pipeline).
Primary emphasis on embeddings index + learned reranker to improve precision on short clinical queries (e.g., 'post-op transfusion complication 72h').
Throughput target: 50k queries/day for clinic network, burst to 500 qps during morning rounds; project potential growth to 100k qps/day in 18 months.
Latency SLOs: 90th percentile end-to-end <200ms for single-patient queries; reranker step P50 <20ms when running on dedicated hardware.
Cost sensitivity: procurement wants modeled cost-per-query at current and 3x scale to compare against Pinecone + custom reranker baseline.
poc_details: POC scope: 1) ingest anonymized 300M medical notes (~200M vectors) 2) run live queries with production-like UI 3) measure latency/cost and verify audit logging.
Vector dims: 1536 (team uses Bio+ clinical embedding variant).
Index footprint: expected ~2.4 TB after compression/quantization; asking about Redwood quantization recommendations and expected RAM/GPU requirements.
Rerank approach: candidate retrieval top-100 via ANN, then neural rerank top-10 on GPU with KV cache warm-up experiments.
POC metrics to deliver: recall@10, rerank latency histogram, tokens-per-second cost, end-to-end 95th percentile latency under realistic QPS.
security_review_notes: Infosec wants explicit audit trail for every retrieval (who/what/query/reply) with 7-year retention for audit logs.
Must support customer-managed KMS or HSM for encryption keys; no persistent plaintext PHI out of VPC.
Network: private peering + strict egress rules; cannot allow any data to transit public internet for PHI traffic.
Legal: BAA required; want example BAA and prior customer reference in healthcare (anonymized OK).
Ask: demonstration of per-request access logs and SSO integration (SAML) with role-based access control for debug endpoints.
commercial_notes: Budget window: fiscal Q2 2026; procurement expects 3 vendor bids (Redwood, Pinecone+custom, Elastic managed).
They prefer committed reserved capacity (Dedicated) if unit economics beat hosted per-query costs at projected volumes.
Key negotiation levers: committed burst capacity, pricing per embedding vector ingest, and discounted rerank GPU-hours.
AE note: focus first on demonstrating stable latency at target scale; cost modeling to follow once we have reliable throughput numbers.
